detail.longDescription: The Power of Decentralization (and Self-Hosting) AI image The Power of Decentralization (and Self-Hosting) Most social networks live inside a single company's servers. One owner, one policy, one point of failure. Decentralization changes that. Instead of one central platform, the network is made of many independent servers — called instances — that talk to each other using open protocols like ActivityPub . You pick your server, keep your identity, and can still follow and interact with people on other servers. It's like email: you use Gmail, I use a private server, and we still reach each other. Why it matters No single point of failure — if one server goes down, the rest of the network keeps running. You own your account — your identity isn't locked inside one company. Real choice — pick a server with rules and a community that fit you. Censorship resistance — no single entity can silence the whole network. Longevity — communities survive even when individual servers come and go. Why self-hosting matters Decentralization is only as real as the people willing to run their own nodes . When you self-host, you don't just use the network — you are the network. Everything runs on hardware you control, with your own rules, your own data, and no third party in the middle. Full control — you decide the software, the policies, the upgrades. Data stays with you — no cloud provider owns or scans your community. Independence — no monthly fees to a platform, no sudden shutdowns. Learning by doing — you understand the stack you depend on. A stronger whole — every self-hosted node makes the network more resilient and harder to break. Decentralization isn't just a technical detail. It's a shift of power from platforms back to people — and self-hosting is how you take that power. About niwego.com: this instance is fully self-hosted and has been running for more than 2 years . It runs on nothing more than an old HP ProDesk 600 G4 Mini PC — no data center, no cloud, no huge budget. Just a small box in a home, proving that the decentralized, self-hosted web is real, sustainable, and within everyone's reach. # Decentralization # SelfHosted # SelfHosting # Fediverse # Friendica # ActivityPub # OpenSource # Privacy # DataSovereignty # HomeLab # IndieWeb # niwego
